raw_case_text:
Patient 2 was a 3-year-old girl who presented with 3 days of continuous high fever, intermittent abdominal pain, vomiting, and retroorbital headache. There had been one episode of gum bleeding on the first day of illness. She had been apparently a well child without any significant illnesses in the past. WBC count done on day 2, on request of the general practitioner, was 8.15 x 103 with 85% neutrophils and platelet count was 120,000 mm3. She had right hypochondrial tenderness with just palpable liver on day 5. ALT and AST were 16 mEq/L and 69.7 mEq/L, respectively, on day 3 and they increased to 29.7 mEq/L and 122.2 mEq/L on day 5. Initial C-reactive protein was 6 mg/dL and remained normal. She was monitored for vital signs including urine output and packed cell volume (PCV). Baseline PCV was 32 and the highest noted was 35. The lowest platelet count documented was 67,000/mm3 and the lowest WBC count was 2.27 x 103. She did not show signs of fluid leakage. However, there was a second episode of gum bleeding on day 5 with normal clotting profile (INR: 1.1 and APTT: 35). She was positive for IgM and negative for IgG antibodies for dengue virus.
On the 5th day of illness, she developed tremors in her upper limbs. She had cogwheel rigidity, mask like face, and staccato speech. Power was grade four in all four limbs with normal reflexes. CT scan of brain revealed diffuse hypodense areas in bilateral basal ganglia and thalamus with predominant involvement of right side (Figure 2). During the first 48 hours after the onset of neurological symptoms, she showed rapid deterioration and became aphasic with severe paucity of movements. Cerebrospinal fluid examination showed 2 lymphocytes without any polymorphs and normal proteins. She recovered dramatically and showed complete recovery within 3 weeks after onset of illness.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 3-year-old girl presenting with a 3-day history of continuous high fever, intermittent abdominal pain, vomiting, retro-orbital headache, and gum bleeding.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 3-year-old girl presented with 3 days of continuous high fever, intermittent abdominal pain, vomiting, and retro-orbital headache, accompanied by an episode of gum bleeding on day 1. On illness day 5, she experienced a second episode of gum bleeding and acutely developed upper limb tremors, cogwheel rigidity, mask-like facies, and staccato speech, rapidly deteriorating over the subsequent 48 hours into aphasia and severe paucity of movement. No clinical signs of plasma leakage were observed.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously well child with no significant illnesses in the past.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for continuous fever, abdominal pain, vomiting, headache, gum bleeding, tremors, rigidity, and loss of speech. Medications and allergies: null.

objective.physical_examination: Day 5: Right hypochondrial tenderness with a palpable liver edge. Neurological examination: Upper extremity tremors, cogwheel rigidity, mask-like face, staccato speech progressing to aphasia and severe paucity of movements; motor power grade 4/5 across all four limbs with preserved normal deep tendon reflexes. Vital signs stable without fluid leakage.
objective.routine_investigations: Day 2: WBC 8.15 x 10^3/muL (85% neutrophils), platelets 120,000/mm3. Day 3: ALT 16 mEq/L, AST 69.7 mEq/L. Day 5: Lowest platelets 67,000/mm3, lowest WBC 2.27 x 10^3/muL, ALT 29.7 mEq/L, AST 122.2 mEq/L, CRP 6 mg/dL (normal), coagulation profile: INR 1.1, aPTT 35 sec. Packed cell volume (PCV): Baseline 32%, peak 35%.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain CT scan: Diffuse hypodense areas in bilateral basal ganglia and thalamus with predominant involvement of the right side. Lumbar puncture / CSF examination: 2 lymphocytes, 0 polymorphonuclear cells, normal protein concentration.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Acute dengue encephalitis / parkinsonian neurodengue presenting with extrapyramidal features (cogwheel rigidity, tremors, mask-like facies, mutism) and bilateral basal ganglia/thalamic CT hypodensities. Diagnostic confirmation: Positive dengue virus IgM antibodies and negative IgG antibodies, confirming primary acute dengue infection; CSF pleocytosis absent with normal protein.
Plan & Outcome: Supportive management with close clinical monitoring of vital signs and fluid balance. Neurological signs resolved dramatically, leading to complete clinical and neurological recovery within 3 weeks of illness onset.
